correctness.rationale: For a strictly positive periodic orbit, integrating the exact logarithmic derivative of S over one period gives <beta_bar I>=bK<1/S>-b. Decomposing the left side into beta<I>+Cov(beta_bar,I), then subtracting the positive averaged-equilibrium identity beta I*=bK/S*-b, gives the first formula with no approximation. The second formula follows analogously from the period average of d log I/dt and subtraction of beta S*+lambda R*=alpha+b. All divisions and quantifiers are explicitly covered by strict positivity; no numerical experiment is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The source explicitly investigates whether an averaged endemic equilibrium approximates mean prevalence of a seasonal orbit and concludes from simulations that the approximation is parameter-dependent. The exact identity isolates the two competing mechanisms controlling infected-prevalence error—reciprocal susceptible level and transmission–infection covariance—and gives a necessary-and-sufficient equality condition. This is a structurally useful diagnostic for an expressly motivated modeling question, not a parameter substitution or a recomputation of a published table.
